title: Department Rule on One Unemployment Insurance Tax Account per Employer
content:
**Rule.** Under the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, an employer holds a single unemployment insurance tax account for all of its Lakeland locations, keyed to its Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN). The number of open accounts per employer is 1.

1. Related businesses that have their own FEIN register their own accounts. They are linked to one another only through a transfer of experience.
2. A new account is registered only when the employer has no other account with status registered, active, delinquent or inactive.
3. An employer whose earlier account is closed registers a new account. The experience of the closed account carries over to the new one only through a transfer of experience under the successorship rules.

## Basis of the registration test

- **What is checked.** The Department's own account records for the same employer: every other account held by that employer and its status. What the employer says about its other accounts does not replace the record.
- **When it is checked.** Before the new account is registered.
- **Which accounts count.** Accounts of the same employer. A related business with its own FEIN is a different employer for this test.

## Status table for the registration test

| Status of the employer's other account | New account may be registered under clause 2 |
|---|---|
| Registered | No |
| Active | No |
| Delinquent | No |
| Inactive | No |
| Closed | Not barred by clause 2; clause 3 applies |
| No other account | Not barred by clause 2 |

**Hypothetical cases.**
- An employer whose only account is inactive asks for a new account for a second Lakeland location. Clause 2 bars it: the inactive account is still the employer's one account, and it covers every Lakeland location.
- An employer whose earlier account is closed starts trading again. It registers a new account (clause 3). The closed account's experience reaches the new account only through a transfer of experience.
